newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Menem's ex-wife abandons sit-in in disgust.
newsitem.headline: Menem's ex-wife abandons sit-in in disgust.

text.p: Argentina's former first lady ended a two-day sit-in protest at police headquarters early on Friday, accusing her ex-husband President Carlos Menem of caring more for power than for their dead son.

Zulema Yoma camped out for two days in a police office in an attempt to force Menem to come and make police hand over a forensic report into their 26-year-old son's death in 1995. She says the report will show that Carlos Jr.'s helicopter was hit by sniper fire before it smashed into a power cable.

But Menem, who says his son's death was an accident, refused to be embarrassed into showing up. His lawyers have effectively delayed the release of the report by asking Bell Helicopters for technical data on the crashed chopper.

"As a father, he should have come. But he did not and so I am leaving," Yoma told a crowd of reporters early on Friday as she abandoned the police building where she had slept on a makeshift bed in a reception room the night before.
Grim-faced and pale, Yoma promised she would continue her fight to uncover what she claims was a political assassination with murky links to drugs covered up by Argentina's security forces.
Speaking earlier in a live link-up with a television talk show, an emotional Yoma accused Menem of abandoning their dead son, leaving him "an orphan without a father."
"He may well be president of the nation, but...the presidential sash cannot mean more than a son," she said.

Yoma lashed out at Menem's entourage, whom she accused of being callous and drunk with power. "When the remains of Carlitos were lying in the white room of the palace of Olivos, they were eating pizza with champagne, and they were watching football and killing themselves laughing," she said.
Yoma said the judge handling the investigation confessed privately to her that Carlos Jr. was murdered and that investigators had found traces of bullets in the wreckage.
But the original Air Force report wrote off the crash as an accident, saying the chopper was flying low along a highway when it hit a power cable, killing Carlitos and a friend.
The 67-year-old president was devastated by the death of his son. But he does not support Yoma's theory, calling it the product of a mother's grief.
Yoma, who divorced Menem after being thrown out of the palace in 1990, has pushed to have Carlos Jr.'s body exhumed for a second autopsy and the word "accident" removed from the file.

The former first lady's conspiracy theory is gradually gaining acceptance and even the public prosecutor in charge of the case, Amalia Sivori, told a newspaper this week that she was investigating "a possible double homicide."
